cohort: 50 French women aged 18-35 who had a C-section
finding: Mothers who use expressive suppression, a response-focused emotion regulation strategy, are less satisfied with childbirth, and emotion regulation, combined with maternal satisfaction, is negatively associated with posttraumatic stress and depression scores.
mod_finding: Mothers who use expressive suppression, a response-focused emotion regulation strategy, are less satisfied with childbirth.
